preamble: In colloquial French the voiced uvular fricative /ʁ/ is deleted as the second member of a word-final obstruent-liquid cluster: quatre /katʁ/ surfaces as [kat], notre and votre as [nɔt] and [vɔt] before a consonant, cidre as [sid]. The deletion is variable and register-sensitive: rare in careful speech, very frequent in casual Parisian speech, favoured by a following consonant, and a stable sociolinguistic marker across northern metropolitan French.

examples.note: Colloquial pronunciation before a consonant (quatre jours); word-final post-obstruent /ʁ/ deleted.
Informal pronunciation before a consonant; votre 'your' likewise becomes [vɔt].
Variable deletion of post-obstruent /ʁ/ recorded in interview corpora from Nancy and Rennes.
Casual Parisian speech; the liquid of the word-final cluster is absent in most tokens of such nouns.

sources: Brand, S., & Ernestus, M. (2021). Reduction of word-final obstruent-liquid-schwa clusters in Parisian French. Corpus Linguistics and Linguistic Theory, 17(1), 249–285. https://doi.org/10.1515/cllt-2017-0067

Boughton, Z. (2015). Social class, cluster simplification and following context: Sociolinguistic variation in word-final post-obstruent liquid deletion in French. Journal of French Language Studies, 25(1), 1–21. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0959269513000446
